abstract.text: Durable Undo and Redo for Swift apps, with the native editing behavior people expect.

inlineContent.text: Let someone type, undo a few keystrokes, commit an edit, and reopen the document
later with its application history intact. UndoKit coordinates that history;
your app keeps its own model, storage and meaning.

Your host defines the operations your app understands, applies each complete
Undo Group atomically, and stores authoritative outcome receipts with its data.
Register the operation once; editing code receives a typed
handle. Native text bindings use the same operations at editing boundaries.
UndoKit supplies ordering, durable history, native UndoManager routing, draft
journaling and recovery coordination. It does not replace your primary datastore
or turn arbitrary UndoManager callbacks into persistent operations.

abstract.text: Standard AppKit text editing with UndoKit routing for durable document history.
AppKit retains ownership of input, selection, marked text and live Undo callbacks.
A durable promise scoped to one History Generation. State holds protect a
checkpoint and its resources. Detail holds protect complete accepted groups
in an inclusive sequence interval, without extending ordinary Undo depth.
Durable Undo and Redo for Swift apps, with the native editing behavior people expect.
An authoritative domain outcome. A thrown callback or absent receipt is unresolved.
Rejection proves no semantic effect; acceptance covers every member atomically.

Coordinates typed edits, native drafts and recovery for one working History Scope.

A typed capability tied to this session epoch, generation and registered handler.
Keep a native text view and its history binding with the scene’s document presentation.

HistoryOwnership.alt: The application retains one History Session per document scope. Windows and SwiftUI views attach to that session. Typed commands reach the host, which commits domain data and outcome receipts together; UndoKit stores history separately.
